decisions.reason: As a very recent and publicly announced launch with an explicit Q1/2019 rollout path, management is likely to attribute any slow uptake to temporary market-access timing and continue backing this strategically relevant particle-therapy QA product.

This chamber sits squarely in the firm's core dosimetry business, and the recent launch plus visible standalone marketing make withdrawal within a year unlikely despite any early commercial uncertainty.

Because it is a newly launched core measurement product backed by the firm's established technical capabilities and public commitment, management would be inclined to persist rather than reverse course quickly.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is highly consistent with the firm's established customer base and reputation, so escalation of commitment and strategic fit both favor keeping it on the market.

Relative dosimetry is central to routine radiation-therapy QA, and the firm would likely justify continued support by viewing any weak early results as temporary for a recently introduced core product.

This thimble chamber extends the firm's familiar hardware portfolio, and given the sunk development effort and public product-page commitment, management would most likely retain it for at least another year.
